summary: Iran informal mutual pause (announced weekend July 26-27) reshapes the macro environment entering FOMC week: Brent falls from $100.40 to $89.73 (-10.7%), WTI from $90.45 to $83.47 (-7.7%), triggering a major rotation from defense and energy into oil-sensitive longs (cruise, airlines, consumer) while simultaneously threatening the supply-risk premium embedded in long-USO and long-ITA. One expiry closed: long-tbt-warsh (+5.4% partial win; Warsh rate-path thesis validated through Q; reloaded in long-tbt-fomc). Three new positions added: long META (pre-earnings July 29 — differentiated AI-monetization profile vs. GOOGL capex template; oil relief improves digital ad budgets), long CCL (Carnival Corp — $0.40-0.50B annualized fuel cost relief from Brent -$10.67/barrel, consumer sentiment recovery), short XLE (energy ETF — $10/barrel Brent decline reprices XLE forward earnings 10-12% lower before sell-side model revisions). Key watches this week: (1) ITA — defense ETF will face selling pressure on Iran pause; requires TWO consecutive daily closes below $225 to trigger stop, not one; first close today (July 27) counts as close #1 if price falls there; (2) USO — WTI $83.47 remains above the $116 USO stop (roughly WTI $72-73 equivalent), but a sustained pause would reduce that buffer; (3) short-JETS — airlines are beneficiaries of lower fuel costs, watch for JETS ETF bouncing from $29.32 toward $35 stop; (4) FOMC July 28-29 — hawkish hold expected with September hike probability at 82%; statement language on September is the clearing event for the entire rate-path book. 28 active positions total; 3 expire within the next 10 days (PYPL July 30, AMZN near stop at $228).

closed_today.note: TBT rose from the $35.50 entry midpoint to $37.40 as Warsh hawkishness and September hike repricing drove 10Y yields toward 4.71% and September hike probability from 33% to 82%. T1 ($39) was not reached before the July 25 expiry. The Warsh rate-path thesis fully validated and was reloaded in long-tbt-fomc-july28-hawkish-stagflation-2026-07-24.
